title_en: SEC’s Brian Daly Provides an Update on Novel ETFs
title_zh: SEC 的 Brian Daly 解读新型 ETF 进展：与 Paul Biaki、Johnny Wu 同场
subtitle_zh: SEC 解读新型 ETF 立规，实物资产与 AI 瓶颈投资
summary_zh: 本期 ETF Prime 由三段访谈组成。首先，SEC 投资管理司司长 Brian Daly 就新型（novel）ETF 的最新进展做更新：自 2019 年 ETF 规则（Rule 6c-11）简化发行流程以来，ETF 数量从约两千只增至近六千只、外壳资产从约四万亿增至十六万亿美元，但行业的创业速度已跑在监管前面。SEC 六月就预测市场、杠杆、单一个股、加密货币及持有私募资产的 ETF 公开征询意见，征询期已关闭，收到约八十五份来件，意见集中在流程速度、申报数量与资产中性三方面；他坦言不愿充当“谁先上市”的裁判，正内部积极讨论、力求拿出合理且可预期的方案。随后 SS&C Alps 的 Paul Biaki 主张当前应最关注实物资产与大宗商品，认为顽固高企的能源价格和“万物电气化”这一长期主题会给通胀带来持久上行压力，并借 SDCI、JCRX、CCNR、EQL、IDOG 等产品阐述如何分散集中度、捕捉市场拓宽与发达市场机会。最后，XETFs 创始人 Johnny Wu 以互联网泡沫作比，讲述其 AI Bottlenecks ETF（NECK）如何用一个代码买入存储、光学光子、电力等瓶颈环节，并解释 Nvidia、Tesla 每日收益 ETF 按日卖权、保留隔夜溢价的机制。

turns.en: So when someone has a great new idea, it goes up on our Edgar system, we have copycat filings for every good new idea at this point within hours. All right, joining me will be Brian Daley, director of the Division of Investment Management at the Securities and Exchange Commission, the SEC,

So everything from whether they should be regulated under the Investment Company Act, to what the SEC's approval process should look like, they floated the possibility of confidential ETF filings.

turns.en: So let me first welcome in, Brian Daley, director of the Division of Investment Management at the SEC. He's joining me from Washington, DC. Brian, it is a pleasure to connect. Welcome to the podcast. Well, thanks for having me. Happy to be here. All right, so I thought, let's first set the backdrop here.
turns.zh: 那就让我先欢迎 Brian Daly，SEC 投资管理司司长，他从华盛顿特区连线加入我们。Brian，很高兴与你交流，欢迎来到本播客。——嗯，谢谢邀请，很高兴来到这里。——好，我想我们先来铺一下背景。

turns.en: And I'll tell you, I know many listeners of this podcast are certainly familiar with a so-called ETF rule. Rule 611, that was implemented in 2019 to help streamline ETF launches, where basically instead of having to request exemptive relief on every filing, there was a framework put in place that simplified the approval process.
turns.zh: 我跟你说，我知道本播客的很多听众当然都熟悉所谓的 ETF 规则（ETF Rule，即 Rule 6c-11），它于 2019 年实施，用来简化 ETF 的发行流程——基本上，你不必再为每一份申报去申请豁免性救济（exemptive relief），而是有了一套简化审批流程的框架。

turns.en: And this did not apply to every type of ETF, but I would say it did cast a pretty wide net. And so let's start there, because I think that'll help set the table for our conversation around novel ETFs. Maybe talk about the impact of that rule and some of the other regulatory reforms we've seen in the ETF space, like the derivatives rule.
turns.zh: 这并不适用于每一种 ETF，但我得说，它确实撒了一张相当宽的网。所以我们就从这里开始，因为我觉得这有助于为我们关于新型 ETF 的对话搭好台子。也许可以谈谈那条规则的影响，以及我们在 ETF 领域见过的其他一些监管改革，比如衍生品规则（derivatives rule）。

turns.en: Well, thanks for having me again. Before I answer, I just have to tell everybody that I am speaking here in my own personal capacity as a division's director, and I don't speak for the chairman, the other commissioners, the commission itself, or my colleagues. But with that, I think that you got the right word.
turns.zh: 嗯，再次感谢邀请。在回答之前，我必须告诉大家：我在这里是以一名司长的个人身份发言，我不代表主席、其他委员、委员会本身或我的同事们。话虽如此，我觉得你用对了那个词。

turns.en: You used the word streamlined. And 611 essentially was a streamlining of a process. Having a process that could take an application from application stage to effectiveness without having to go to individual staff members for exemptive orders, made the ETF viable in a way it never was before.
turns.zh: 你用了“简化”（streamlined）这个词。6c-11 本质上就是对流程的一次简化。有了一套能让申请从申报阶段走到生效阶段、而不必逐个去找工作人员申请豁免令的流程，让 ETF 变得前所未有地可行。

turns.en: And it was able to access and address the retail market in a way we've never seen before. It's good government at its best. And the numbers bear that out, right? We went from around 2000 to just under 6,000 ETFs out there in just a few years. The AUM of the ETF wrapper went from about 4 trillion to about 16, so 4x there.
turns.zh: 它得以用一种我们前所未见的方式去接触并服务零售市场。这是“善政”（good government）的最佳典范。数字也印证了这一点，对吧？短短几年间，我们从大约 2000 只 ETF 增长到接近 6000 只。ETF 这个外壳（wrapper）的资产管理规模从约 4 万亿美元增长到约 16 万亿，翻了 4 倍。

turns.en: And we right now look at in the division about 125 ETFs going effective or fund IPOs every month at this point. So clearly the wrapper works. Clearly the process helps. And we really want to make sure that we continue to support innovation and put more choices out there for the retail investor. Okay, so that's perfect.
turns.zh: 而我们司里现在看到的大约是每个月有 125 只 ETF 生效或完成基金首发（fund IPO）。所以显然，这个外壳是有效的，这个流程是有帮助的。我们真的想确保继续支持创新，为零售投资者提供更多选择。——好，这太完美了。

turns.en: Clearly there's been tremendous ETF growth and innovation over the past seven years since the ETF rule. And I will tell you from my perspective, Brian, it seemed like the ETF industry was sort of outrunning regulators ability to keep up with that. And that's certainly not a negative statement on the SEC. It's much more a statement on,
turns.zh: 显然，自 ETF 规则以来的过去七年里，ETF 出现了巨大的增长和创新。我跟你说，从我的角度看，Brian，ETF 行业似乎有点跑在了监管者跟进能力的前面。这当然不是对 SEC 的负面评价，更多是在说——

turns.en: let's call out the entrepreneurial spirit of the ETF industry. And so back at the end of June, early July, as I noted at the top, the SEC did put out this request for public comment on novel ETFs, which I saw is a way to attempt to address how your agency handles the speed of innovation. Is that fair or you tell us why did the SEC
turns.zh: 我们就叫它 ETF 行业的创业精神（entrepreneurial spirit）吧。所以回到 6 月底、7 月初，正如我开头提到的，SEC 确实就新型 ETF 发布了这份公众意见征询。我把它看作是你们机构试图应对创新速度的一种方式。这么说公道吗？还是你来告诉我们，SEC 为什么

turns.en: put out this request for a public comment? I think you got it right. We are looking at new assets in the ETF wrapper. We're looking at new structures being used and put into the ETF wrapper. And a lot of innovation out there, often responding to demand. At the same time, we have what you talk about a lot, the ETF terror domes out there.
turns.zh: 要发布这份公众意见征询？——我觉得你说对了。我们在关注 ETF 外壳里的新资产，在关注被放进 ETF 外壳里的新结构。外面有大量创新，往往是对需求的回应。与此同时，我们又有你经常谈到的那种 ETF“角斗场”。

turns.en: And it is undeniable that in many cases, the first to market, the first to hit the market and gather significant assets, wins, and there is no second place. And that is simply a market reality. It's not good or bad, it just is the reality. But when we are charged with reviewing these applications when they come in,
turns.zh: 而且不可否认，在很多情况下，第一个上市、第一个打进市场并聚集起可观资产的人赢者通吃，没有第二名。这纯粹就是一个市场现实。它无所谓好坏，它就是现实。但当我们被要求去审查这些送进来的申请时，

turns.en: now puts a lot of pressure on us, on the fund sponsor, on the fund sponsor's council. And as you noted earlier, our process is public. So when someone has a great new idea, it goes up on our Edgar system, we have copycat filings for every good new idea at this point within hours. And the pressure for the sponsor
turns.zh: 这就给我们、给基金发起人、给发起人的法律顾问带来了很大压力。而且正如你刚才提到的，我们的流程是公开的。所以当有人冒出一个绝妙的新点子，它一上传到我们的 EDGAR 系统，几个小时之内每一个好点子都会招来跟风申报。而对于那个

turns.en: who came up with the novel idea is tremendous because they want to preserve, it was their idea, they want to get to market first. Everyone else who wants to, brings to market wants to get to market with them or maybe ahead of them. And our staff is left with this situation, which is somewhat undeniable of having to be the arbiter.
turns.zh: 想出新点子的发起人来说，压力是巨大的，因为他们想保住——那是他们的点子，他们想第一个上市。其他所有想把它推向市场的人，都想跟他们同时、甚至抢在他们前面上市。而我们的工作人员就被置于这种某种程度上无法回避的境地：不得不充当那个“裁判”。

turns.en: You have a regulator as the arbiter of which sponsor gets to market first. And that's the place we don't want to be. It's a place the sponsors don't want us to be in the public. If they thought about it, it wouldn't want us there either. So the purpose in large part, most of what was behind that ETFRFC was a desire to talk to the industry
turns.zh: 你让一个监管者去裁判哪个发起人能第一个上市。而那正是我们不想处的位置，也是发起人不希望我们处的位置，公众如果想过这件事，也不会希望我们处在那儿。所以那份 ETF 意见征询（ETF RFC）背后的目的，很大程度上是想跟业界谈谈，

turns.en: and get ideas and how to make sure we have an orderly and predictable process to let people get good new novel ideas to market in a way that still allows for collaboration and intelligent discussion with these sponsors, which we don't have today. Okay, so you did want to talk to the industry
turns.zh: 听听想法，看看怎样才能确保我们有一个有序、可预期的流程，让人们能以一种仍然允许与这些发起人协作、进行明智讨论的方式，把好点子、新点子推向市场——而这种讨论我们今天是没有的。——好，所以你确实想跟业界谈谈，

turns.en: and I noted the formal public comment period is now closed. So I'm curious what's been your initial reaction to the industry's response? Is there anything in particular standing out to you in your staff as you begun parsing through the comments? So we got about 85 letters and inbound. Some of the inbounds were discussions.
turns.zh: 而我也注意到正式的公众意见征询期现在已经结束了。所以我很好奇，你对业界的回应最初的反应是什么？在你和你的工作人员开始梳理这些意见时，有没有什么特别突出的东西？——我们收到了大约 85 封信件和各种来件。有些来件是交流讨论。

turns.en: They're very much welcomed. I would say about two-thirds of those had a lot of substance and detail. But what we really liked about this was about a third of our inbounds came from sponsors and there is no substitute for talking to the people who are actually putting these products together who are putting risk on the line
turns.zh: 这些都非常受欢迎。我得说，其中大约三分之二有相当多的实质内容和细节。但我们真正喜欢的一点是：大约三分之一的来件来自发起人。跟那些真正在把这些产品组装起来、把风险押上去的人交谈，是无可替代的，

turns.en: and that was really welcomed. There were, if I had to put it in a couple of buckets, there were four basic themes that came through. The first one was almost unanimous. Everyone hated the term novel ETF so don't, we're not going to stick on that but people did not like that label. On the substantive side, it was clear in terms of speed,
turns.zh: 这一点非常受欢迎。如果我要把它归成几个桶，那么浮现出来的基本主题有四个。第一个几乎是一致意见：所有人都讨厌“新型 ETF”（novel ETF）这个词，所以我们不会沿用它——大家都不喜欢那个标签。在实质层面，就速度而言很清楚：

turns.en: no one likes legal gamesmanship and the sponsors came out hard and strong with support for us to have a transparent process that was understandable. Ordinary and predictable outcomes are what everybody seems to want and we would agree with that. In terms of volume, it is clear that the spaghetti cannon which you talk about a lot as well
turns.zh: 没人喜欢法律上的钻空子（legal gamesmanship），发起人们态度鲜明、强烈地支持我们拥有一个透明、可理解的流程。“普通、可预期的结果”似乎是每个人都想要的，我们也认同这一点。就数量而言，很清楚，你也常谈到的那门“意面炮”（spaghetti cannon）

turns.en: is alive and well and continuing to grow. People don't have concerns about the spaghetti cannon itself. They have concerns that spaghetti cannon processes are taking staff time away from looking at novel things that require more and more thinking and that's certainly a valid concern. We would agree with that concern.
turns.zh: 依然活跃、还在持续增长。人们担心的并不是“意面炮”本身，他们担心的是“意面炮”式的流程占用了工作人员的时间，让他们没法去看那些需要越来越多思考的新型东西——这当然是一个合理的担忧，我们也认同。

turns.en: And in terms of new assets, there's a concern that people want to make sure that we will continue to be asset neutral. And really, if you put those together, those are the three categories that people had substantive concerns about. Okay, so before I let you go then, what's next in this process? Where does everything stand now
turns.zh: 而在新资产方面，大家担心的是希望确保我们会继续保持“资产中性”（asset neutral）。真的，如果你把这些放在一起，那就是人们在实质层面有担忧的三个类别。——好，那在放你走之前，这个流程接下来会怎样？现在一切进展到哪一步，

So unfortunately, for your listeners and viewers, what we do is by necessity confidential, so we can't really share with it. Other than I can say, we are having active discussions internally, every office and every division is involved,
turns.zh: 接下来又会走向何方？——我们正在内部非常积极地讨论。所以很遗憾，对你的听众和观众来说，我们做的事情出于必要是保密的，所以我们没法真的分享。我只能说：我们正在内部积极讨论，每个办公室、每个司都参与其中，

turns.en: we have a lot of white boarding of things to do we think we're getting reasonably close to putting proposals together for the commission to think about. I eat up going up to the chairman. turns.zh: 我们做了大量的白板推演（white boarding）。我们认为自己正相当接近于把一些提案整理出来，供委员会思考。我也会向上呈报给主席。我们真正希望的，只是大家会相信：我们最终拿出来的东西会是合理的、

turns.en: that is subjective, that is asset neutral, and that will be workable and continue that theme of good government that we've had. We need a little more time to get that together. I think people understand that, but that's basically where we are. Well, Brian, thank you for providing an update this week. I know everybody in the industry

turns.zh: 有没有什么让你印象深刻的地方？——没有，本着让彼此都感觉良好的精神，我觉得你把一些信息从他那儿套出来，做得非常出色。我认为这是一次很棒的访谈。你说到 ETF 行业的创业精神时，真是一针见血，

turns.en: and the pressure that can put on regulators and has put on regulators historically. And my sense is the goal is to get to some level of clarity. And clarity is good for market participants. It's good for issuers. It's good for allocators. It's good for advisors. It's good for people who interact with the ETF wrapper.
turns.zh: 以及它可能给监管者带来的、并且历来确实带来的压力。我的感觉是，目标是达到某种程度的清晰度（clarity）。而清晰度对市场参与者是好事，对发行人是好事，对配置方是好事，对投顾是好事，对所有跟 ETF 外壳打交道的人都是好事。

turns.en: And so given that the pace of innovation has been so swift, the number of ETF launches once again in 2026 is on pace to set another record. The fact that so many different types of strategies spanning so many different asset classes are being tried by ETF issuers. In some cases, perhaps pushing the envelope
turns.zh: 所以，鉴于创新的步伐如此之快——2026 年 ETF 发行数量又一次有望刷新纪录；鉴于如此多不同类型、横跨如此多不同资产类别的策略正被 ETF 发行人尝试，在某些情况下，也许是在以一种

turns.en: in a way that we didn't see maybe 15 years ago in the ETF wrapper, I think is exciting for the future of the ETF industry. But at the same time, speaks to the challenge that Mr. Daily faces. And he seems to be up for it and is very deliberate and considerate in how he's approaching it. So I found a very reassuring
turns.zh: 我们也许 15 年前在 ETF 外壳里没见到的方式去挑战极限——我觉得这对 ETF 行业的未来是令人兴奋的。但与此同时，它也说明了 Daly 先生面临的挑战。而他似乎乐于迎接，并且在如何处理上非常审慎、周到。所以我觉得很令人安心，

turns.en: that we've got a guy at the helm who clearly understands the industry very well, understands the importance of the wrapper. And if I could take anything away from what he said, one of the things I pulled out of there was the idea that the ETF wrapper has won. It's at the point now where it's just not debatable.
turns.zh: 掌舵的这个人显然非常了解这个行业，了解这个外壳的重要性。如果要从他说的话里带走点什么，我从中提炼出的一点是：ETF 外壳已经赢了。它已经到了不再需要争论的地步。

turns.en: The future trajectory of the ETF. But we have to make sure that that trajectory is on a path that's in the best interest of both issuers and investors. I think all of that is really well said, Paul. And I think about just from my perspective in covering the ETF space. And I've mentioned this multiple times on the podcast.
turns.zh: ETF 的未来轨迹已经确定。但我们必须确保这条轨迹走在一条对发行人和投资者都最有利的道路上。——我觉得这些都说得非常好，Paul。而我从我自己报道 ETF 领域的角度想了想，我在播客里也多次提到过这一点。

turns.en: I can't keep up with everything happening in the space. I try to keep up on new launches and filings and everything occurring. And I can't do it. So I can only imagine a regulator who has to make sure these products are coming to market in the right way. And they do have this mandate of making sure
turns.zh: 我根本跟不上这个领域正在发生的一切。我努力去跟上新发行、新申报和正在发生的所有事情，可我做不到。所以我只能想象，一个必须确保这些产品以正确方式上市的监管者——而且他们确实肩负着确保

turns.en: there's the proper investor protections in place. That's a tough job when you have the type of innovation we have in the ETF space. And so I don't envy their situation, but I agree with you. It certainly seems like Brian and his staff are up to the task here. And I appreciate them trying to continue to put a robust framework in place
turns.zh: 有适当投资者保护措施到位的职责——在我们 ETF 领域这种创新程度下，那是份艰难的工作。所以我不羡慕他们的处境，但我同意你的看法。Brian 和他的团队显然确实看起来能胜任。我很感激他们努力继续搭建一个稳健的框架，

turns.en: for how all this innovation occurs. Because you said it perfectly. The ETF wrapper has won. And now we're seeing issuers and we see new issuers every day push the envelope of that wrapper, which I think is a good thing. That's entrepreneurialism. But it's certainly a challenge. So anyway, we can move on. I appreciate your comments.
turns.zh: 来规范所有这些创新如何发生。因为你说得再准确不过了：ETF 外壳已经赢了。而现在我们看到发行人——我们每天都看到新发行人——去挑战这个外壳的极限，我觉得这是好事，那是创业精神。但它当然是个挑战。好了，我们往下走，谢谢你的评论。

turns.en: I just, as somebody who, again, is operating in the space, you're thinking about innovation and new products. I really wanted to hear your take on that. So let's get into the current financial markets. We'll pivot here. And we'll talk about some themes to watch in Q4. And also some potential portfolio considerations.
turns.zh: 我只是——作为一个同样在这个领域里运作、在思考创新和新产品的人——我真的很想听听你对那点的看法。那我们来聊聊当前的金融市场，我们在这里转个向。我们会谈谈四季度（Q4）值得关注的一些主题，以及一些潜在的组合考量。

turns.en: And obviously, there is a lot going on right now. But let me start with this, Paul. If you had to pick one area that investors and advisors should be thinking about right now, one area, what would be at the top of your list? Well, I think it's real assets. It's something we're extremely passionate about.
turns.zh: 显然，现在有很多事情在发生。但让我先问这个，Paul：如果让你挑出投资者和投顾现在应该思考的一个领域，就一个，什么会排在你清单的最顶端？——嗯，我觉得是实物资产（real assets）。这是我们极其热衷的东西。

turns.en: And in many ways, real assets can map to different headline flow at the moment. So we're going to get CPI and PPI this week. Of course, inflation is still very much top of mind for the market. It's very much top of mind for the Fed. As we've seen from the recent Fed minutes and the recent perhaps unexpected hike,
turns.zh: 而且在很多方面，实物资产可以对应上眼下不同的头条与资金流。所以我们这周会拿到 CPI 和 PPI。当然，通胀仍然是市场非常挂心的事，也是美联储非常挂心的事。正如我们从最近的美联储会议纪要、以及最近那次也许出乎意料的加息中所看到的——

turns.en: not necessarily unexpected in the sense that the market wasn't pricing in a hike. The market was very much pricing in a hike at the last meeting. But unexpected in terms of where we were at the beginning of the year and what the expectation was around Fed policy. Remember, at the beginning of the year,
turns.zh: 说它出乎意料，并不是说市场没在为加息定价；上次会议市场是非常在为加息定价的。出乎意料是相对于我们年初所处的位置、以及当时对美联储政策的预期而言。记住，年初时，

turns.en: the expectation was that we were going to get a couple cuts here in 2026. And then, of course, we embark upon this conflict in Iran and that changes the calculus from an inflation perspective. And I do think, as it relates to the impact of potentially higher than expected inflation on portfolios, a lot of advisors and a lot of investors
turns.zh: 大家的预期是我们 2026 年会降息几次。然后，当然，我们卷入了伊朗这场冲突，那就从通胀的角度改变了整个盘算。而我确实觉得，就潜在的、高于预期的通胀对组合的影响而言，很多投顾和很多投资者

turns.en: are ill-equipped to insulate their portfolios from the impact of inflation. And the reason is is because the asset classes that typically do best in an inflationary environment, commodities to a degree of real estate are typically under owned by investors. And so our argument in many ways is, in the near term, we've got this uncertainty
turns.zh: 都没有做好准备去保护自己的组合免受通胀冲击。原因在于：那些在通胀环境里通常表现最好的资产类别——某种程度上的大宗商品、房地产——通常都被投资者低配（under owned）。所以我们的论点在很多方面是：短期内，我们面临着这种围绕

turns.en: around the pace of inflation and the expectation, depending on where you look, is that inflation is going to remain sticky above the Fed's target. And there's potential given the level of diesel prices and the way that works through the economy, the elevated level of WTI and Brent, Brent, up over $100 a barrel, WTI, up over $90 a barrel.
turns.zh: 通胀节奏的不确定性，而预期——取决于你看哪里——是通胀将会顽固地停留在美联储目标之上。而且鉴于柴油价格的水平、以及它如何传导到整个经济，加上 WTI 和 Brent 的高企——Brent 涨破每桶 100 美元，WTI 涨破每桶 90 美元——

turns.en: In an environment where you have stubbornly high energy prices, you have stubbornly high refined product prices, that puts, I would say, durable upward pressure on inflation. And we know from history that in that environment, commodities provide a really important portfolio component. They've typically done very well
turns.zh: 在一个能源价格顽固高企、成品油价格顽固高企的环境里，我会说，这给通胀带来了持久的上行压力。而从历史中我们知道，在那种环境里，大宗商品提供了一个非常重要的组合成分。它们通常在

turns.en: and higher than expected inflationary environments. Naturally, commodities provide investors with a view on future inflation. But then you extend beyond the near term horizon to some of the knock-on effects of the war in Iran, as well as the inflationary environment we're in and some of the infrastructure spending
turns.zh: 高于预期的通胀环境里表现非常好。自然地，大宗商品给投资者提供了一个关于未来通胀的视角。但如果你把视野延伸到近期之外，去看看伊朗战争的一些连锁影响、以及我们所处的通胀环境和一些基础设施支出，

turns.en: and some of the other key themes in the marketplace. And what we see long-term is upward pressure on commodity prices as a result of an imbalance between supply and demand. And so if I were to sum all that up, Nate, it would be that commodities have a really important role in an asset allocation framework.
turns.zh: 还有市场里其他一些关键主题，我们长期看到的是：由于供需之间的失衡，大宗商品价格面临上行压力。所以如果让我把这一切总结一下，Nate，那就是：大宗商品在资产配置框架里扮演着一个非常重要的角色。

turns.en: Most advisors, most allocators don't have any exposure to commodities. And what makes commodities such a powerful tool in a portfolio is first of all, they're inherently a diversifier. They have low correlations to the ag. They have low correlations to equities. But the volatility profile of a basket of commodities.
turns.zh: 而大多数投顾、大多数配置方对大宗商品没有任何敞口。让大宗商品成为组合中如此强大工具的，首先是它们天生就是一个分散器（diversifier）。它们跟国债（agg）相关性低，跟股票相关性也低。但一篮子大宗商品的波动率特征——

turns.en: So not an individual commodity like oil or wheat, but when you put them all together, it's very similar to the volatility profile of equity markets. So you get low correlation attritional asset classes with the volatility profile that looks and feels a lot like equity markets when they're packaged together
turns.zh: 注意不是单个大宗商品，比如石油或小麦，而是当你把它们全都放在一起时——非常类似于股票市场的波动率特征。所以当你把它们打包在一起时，你得到的是与主流资产类别低相关性、却有着看起来和感觉起来都很像股票市场的波动率特征，

turns.en: and in our mind, that's a very underutilized portfolio tool. And then you get the long-term structural tailwinds as a result of the massive investment that's going to come out in response to the conflict that I ran. But also some of the upward pressure that's being placed on these commodities markets
turns.zh: 在我们看来，这是一个被严重低估的组合工具。然后你还能得到长期的结构性顺风，源自于为回应伊朗冲突而将要投入的巨额投资，以及我们所见的一切——从电动车（EV）到电气化——给这些大宗商品市场带来的上行压力。

turns.en: as a result of some of the economic evolution that we're seeing around everything from EVs to the electrification. So if I were to summarize what you just said, then it really sounds like inflation should be top of mind for investors and advisors right now. And obviously potential, I'll call them inflation hedges in portfolios.
turns.zh: ……源于我们所见的经济演变，从电动车到电气化，给这些大宗商品市场带来的一些上行压力。——那么如果我总结一下你刚说的，听起来就是：通胀此刻应该是投资者和投顾最挂心的事，显然还有组合里那些——我就叫它们“通胀对冲”（inflation hedges）的工具吧。

turns.en: Is that a fair characterization? Yeah. And I don't want to paint with too broad a brush around how advisors or investors are thinking about inflation. But I do think that because we had that very aggressive wave of inflation a couple years ago to levels we really hadn't seen in decades and then the sort of come down of that inflation
turns.zh: 这么概括公道吗？——是的。我不想用太宽泛的笔触去描述投顾或投资者如何看待通胀。但我确实觉得，因为几年前我们经历了那一波非常凶猛的通胀，涨到了几十年没见过的水平，然后通胀又多少回落——

turns.en: to levels that feel a little bit more manageable, 3%, 3 plus percent, 3.1, whatever the number is on an ongoing basis. There's a level of that complacency that is inherent in that type of cycle whereby you're really worried about inflation when it's 7, 8, 9% annualized. And then when it comes back down to 3%,
turns.zh: 回落到感觉稍微可控一点的水平，3%、3% 出头、3.1%，随便那个数字是多少。在那种周期里，天生就存在一种自满（complacency）：当通胀年化到 7%、8%、9% 时你才真的担心它，而当它回落到 3% 时，

turns.en: it doesn't feel as impactful economically or even socially. But the truth is that if inflation goes from 9% to 3%, it doesn't mean that inflation has gone in the other direction. It just means that it's decelerated. So price levels are higher. And in many ways the perils from a retirement perspective,
turns.zh: 它在经济上、甚至社会上就没那么有冲击力了。但事实是，如果通胀从 9% 降到 3%，并不意味着通胀反向走了，只意味着它减速了。所以价格水平是更高的。而且在很多方面，从退休的角度看，那些隐患——

turns.en: from a future value of money perspective are still there. They're just there in a different way. And so commodities we feel are a really important tool for people who are concerned about their clients' money in retirement, the value of the money in their retirement accounts, and their overall brokerage accounts.
turns.zh: 从货币未来价值的角度看——依然存在，只是以另一种方式存在。所以我们觉得，大宗商品对于那些担心客户退休资金、担心退休账户里货币价值、以及担心整体经纪账户的人来说，是一个非常重要的工具。

turns.en: With an asset class like commodities or other real assets, can you talk a little bit about actual portfolio implementation? Like let's say some investors and advisors are thinking about obtaining exposure here. What is the right or what's the wrong way to go about doing so? Like how do you see this in practice?
turns.zh: 对于像大宗商品或其他实物资产这样的资产类别，你能不能谈谈实际的组合落地（implementation）？比如说，有些投资者和投顾在考虑获取这块敞口，那么正确的做法是什么、错误的做法又是什么？在实践中你是怎么看的？

turns.en: Yeah, so there's been, I think, an evolution and rightfully so in how we think about asset allocation. The 60-40 model has evolved. It's evolved to include privates in some instances in a way that maybe wasn't part of the lexicon say five or 10 years ago. There's also an evolution in terms of what we think
turns.zh: 是的，我觉得我们对资产配置的思考方式一直在演进，而且理当如此。60/40 模型已经演进了。它演进到在某些情况下纳入私募（privates），这是五年前、十年前也许还不在词汇表里的。我们对

turns.en: the role of fixed income is in a portfolio. My argument here is not to say replace the 40% of a 60-40 that's in fixed income with commodities, necessarily. What we're saying is that if you're thinking about a starting point for an asset allocation is 60-40 and you're thinking about how do I ensure that an environment where the correlation
turns.zh: 固定收益在组合中扮演什么角色的思考也在演进。我在这里的论点并不是说，非要把 60/40 里那 40% 的固定收益换成大宗商品。我们说的是：如果你把资产配置的起点设想成 60/40，而你在思考——在一个股票和债券相关性

turns.en: between stocks and bonds is risen, which we've seen over the course of the past four or five years, then how do you go about reconfiguring client assets in a way that insulates you somewhat from the impact of that correlation and commodities in our mind are a diversifier in that way. And so if you're just chipping away
turns.zh: 上升的环境里（我们在过去四五年里已经见到了），我该如何确保……那你该怎样重新配置客户资产，以在某种程度上把自己与那种相关性上升的冲击隔离开来？在我们看来，大宗商品就是那样一个分散器。所以如果你只是

turns.en: at the edges of that asset allocation and incorporating commodities in place of both equities and fixed income, that's how we see advisors implementing commodities. And you look at a product like SDCI, for example, which we distribute on behalf of USCF. It's dynamic, it's not static. It doesn't track the BCOM or the widely followed
turns.zh: 在这个资产配置的边缘一点点地削，把大宗商品同时替换掉一部分股票和一部分固定收益，这就是我们看到的投顾落地大宗商品的方式。你看看像 SDCI 这样的产品，比如——我们代表 USCF 分销它。它是动态的，不是静态的。它不跟踪 BCOM 或那些被广泛跟随的

turns.en: commodities indexes. It rebalances on a monthly basis toward those commodities with better term structures. We've seen that be a very useful tool to affect your commodities view without having to make a call on individual commodity. Now, we've got a mutual fund, JCRX is the ticker, which is a combination of both the futures
turns.zh: 大宗商品指数。它按月向那些期限结构（term structure）更好的商品再平衡。我们发现，这是一个非常有用的工具，能让你表达对大宗商品的观点，而不必对单个商品下判断。另外，我们有一只共同基金，代码 JCRX，它把商品领域里的期货

turns.en: in the commodity space as well as the equities. And we spun out the equity portion of that portfolio into an ETF a few years ago, CCNR is the ticker there. That's another way to take that futures exposure, which again, we argue is an inherent diversifier, but combine it with companies that are typically owned
turns.zh: 和股票结合起来。几年前我们把那个组合里的股票部分拆分出来做成了一只 ETF，代码是 CCNR。那是另一种获取期货敞口的方式——我们同样主张它是天生的分散器——但把它跟那些通常在你分散化资产配置里被持有的公司结合起来。

turns.en: in your diversified asset allocation net as we've talked about previously, the footprint of energy, materials, the companies that are tasked globally with exploring for processing, refining, raw materials, basic materials, energy commodities from upstream to downstream has fallen dramatically over the course of the past 20 years.
turns.zh: 正如我们之前谈到的，能源、材料这些行业——那些在全球范围内负责勘探、加工、提炼原材料、基础材料、能源商品的公司，从上游到下游——在过去 20 年间，它们的占比已经大幅下降。

turns.en: So they're typically underrepresented even in the equity sleeve of an asset allocation. And so what we're talking to advisors about, what we're talking to allocators about is this idea that you typically underrepresented in the industries and sectors tied to commodities markets while also understanding that a lot of advisors
turns.zh: 所以它们即使在资产配置的股票部分里，通常也是被低配的。因此我们跟投顾谈、跟配置方谈的，是这样一个理念：你通常在那些与大宗商品市场挂钩的行业和板块上被低配，同时还要理解，很多投顾

turns.en: simply don't have exposure to the raw materials themselves or the commodities themselves. Okay, so building what I'll call inflation resilient portfolios and perhaps looking to an area like commodities that's clearly a theme that you're tracking. As we look to the remainder of the year, what else is on your radar?
turns.zh: 对原材料本身、或大宗商品本身干脆就没有敞口。——好，所以构建我所说的“抗通胀组合”（inflation resilient portfolios），也许把目光投向像大宗商品这样显然是你正在追踪的一个主题的领域。展望今年剩余时间，你雷达上还有什么？

turns.en: What else do you think investors should be paying attention to? Yeah, so we've talked about it in the past, Nate, this electrification of everything theme, which we think is a multi-decade theme that's gonna play out in front of us, not just in our market lives, but also in our day-to-day lives in the real world
turns.zh: 你觉得投资者还应该关注什么？——是的，我们过去聊过这个，Nate，就是“万物电气化”（electrification of everything）这个主题。我们认为这是一个会持续数十年、将在我们眼前展开的主题，不仅在我们的市场生活里，也在现实世界的日常生活里，

turns.en: because of the implementation of upgraded grids and systems and new technologies to get the type of generation that we need to satisfy this explosion and electricity demand that we're seeing as well as the investment that's gonna take place in the raw materials to support improved transmission and enhanced transmission of electricity
turns.zh: 因为要落实升级的电网和系统、以及新技术，去获得我们需要的那种发电量，来满足我们所见的电力需求爆发；还有为了支持在美国和全球改善输电、增强输电而将在原材料上进行的投资。

turns.en: in the United States and globally. And so in many ways these things tie together, real assets, commodities, real estate, and infrastructure as part of a durable inflation-sensitive asset allocation framework, but also the electrification of everything sort of stepping in as another demand source
